verdict.rationale: Moss is mainly a programmatic product, which makes headless automation natural. It ships Python and TypeScript SDKs (moss-docs-1, moss-docs-8), an HTTP API multiplexed through `/v1/manage` (moss-docs-10), and an official CLI for terminal use and key management (moss-docs-3, moss-docs-21, moss-probe-4). Disk caching and snapshot fallback on 429/503 errors also suit unattended runs (moss-docs-24, moss-docs-25). Missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline documentation (e.g. GitHub Actions examples), documented non-interactive CLI auth (the docs show an interactive-style `moss login`), a published OpenAPI spec (moss-probe-2), and independent hands-on corroboration of CI use.
